### Assistant: During a clear day the sky usually looks blue because air scatters shorter blue wavelengths of sunlight more than longer ones (Rayleigh scattering). ### Assistant: During a clear day the sky usually looks blue because air scatters shorter blue wavelengths of sunlight more than longer ones (Rayleigh scattering). ### Assistant: During a clear day the sky usually looks blue because air scatters shorter blue wavelengths of sunlight more than longer ones (Rayleigh scattering). ### Assistant: During a clear day the sky usually looks blue because air scatters shorter blue wavelengths of sunlight more than longer ones (Rayleigh scattering). ### User: what color is the sky
### Assistant: During a clear day the sky usually looks blue because air scatters shorter blue wavelengths of sunlight more than longer ones (Rayleigh scattering). At sunrise and sunset it can look orange, red, pink, or purple because sunlight travels through more atmosphere and more blue light is scattered away. Cloudy skies look gray or white when many water droplets scatter light in all directions.
